brand_dna.category: Independent family-owned craft brewery in King Valley, Victoria, selling European-style ales and lagers plus merch, direct to Australian drinkers.
brand_dna.core_belief: Beer worth slowing down for - brewing time-honoured styles that have survived for centuries, with no shortcuts and no trends for the sake of trends.
proof_points: 100% independently family owned and operated brewery in King Valley, Victoria
King Valley Kolsch won Bronze at the Australian International Beer Awards 2023, 2024, 2025 & 2026
Mango Berliner Weisse awarded Silver 2022 & Bronze 2023 for Best Fruit Beer at the Australian International Beer Awards
Uses only premium and local ingredients wherever possible, with fresh North East Victorian hops
brand_dna.positioning: Premium, traditional and craft-led - heritage European styles over hype, quality and balance over gimmicks.

voice_pillars.name: Patient Craftsman
voice_pillars.desc: Writes with pride in tradition, patience and technique over speed or trend-chasing.
voice_pillars.quote: No shortcuts. No trends for the sake of trends. Just beers with history, made for today.

voice_pillars.name: Rooted In Place
voice_pillars.desc: Anchors every beer to the King Valley region, its water and its local ingredients.
voice_pillars.quote: showcases the beauty of our region with crisp characters from our super fresh water

voice_pillars.name: Easy And Warm
voice_pillars.desc: Approachable, human language that invites you back for another sip rather than lecturing.
voice_pillars.quote: We call this beer the Elbow Bender as it's so easy to come back for another sip.

voice_pillars.name: Style-Led Confidence
voice_pillars.desc: Speaks plainly about what they do best and lets balance be the flex.
voice_pillars.quote: well balanced beer is our thing

phrases: extremely well balanced and an excellent drop
so easy to come back for another sip
A perfect beer for any occasion
goes down well all year round

icp: Australian craft beer drinkers who value tradition, balance and provenance, and buy premium European-style beer from an independent local brewery they can trust.

personas.name: The Beer Traditionalist
personas.description: Style-literate drinker who appreciates Belgian Tripels, Kolsch and Doppelbocks; moved by heritage, craftsmanship and award pedigree.

personas.name: The Local Loyalist
personas.description: North East Victoria and High Country supporter who backs independent family-owned makers; moved by regional origin and fresh local ingredients.

personas.name: The Easy Sessioner
personas.description: Casual drinker who wants a balanced, refreshing beer for any occasion; moved by 'easy to come back for another sip' approachability.

offers: Brew Crew membership: an incredible box of beer delivered every quarter
Beer sold as Single, 4 Pack and 16 Case options
Mixed Cases and Gift Vouchers available
Flat shipping over $100 ($10 VIC, $15 NSW & ACT); ships to VIC, ACT, NSW, QLD & SA
30-day return policy on eligible items (unworn/unused, with tags, original packaging)

banned.claim: Calling the brand or its packaging 'sustainable' or 'eco-friendly'
banned.why: FTC Green Guides - unqualified sustainability claim with no verifiable backing on site.

banned.claim: Claiming beer or merch is 'carbon neutral' or 'zero impact'
banned.why: FTC Green Guides - no specific, verifiable proof provided.

banned.claim: Describing merch as '100% recycled' or made from recycled materials
banned.why: FTC Green Guides - no material breakdown or verification present.

banned.claim: Any health or medical benefit claim (e.g. beer that 'aids digestion' or 'relieves stress')
banned.why: Unsubstantiated health claim; not supported anywhere on site and off-limits for alcohol.

banned.claim: Marketing beer in a way that encourages excessive or underage drinking
banned.why: Conflicts with the brand's stated responsible service of alcohol commitments and liquor law.

banned.claim: Stating a fixed award count or medal without naming the specific beer and year
banned.why: Awards are beer-specific; a generic 'award-winning brewery' claim overstates verifiable proof.
